messages.subject: ggmap questions
parts:
(Forward on behalf of Roy M)


Hi All:

I am working on getting some biological data, mapping it, and then
adding satellite data using ggmap. Below is R code that should
remotely get the biological and map it using ggmap (see the output
file map_cages2.png, and then remotely get the sea surface temperature
data (sst) and read it into R (this requires ncdf4). It is at this
point that I am stuck. I would like to add the sst data as an "image"
but I am unclear on what other problems ggmap works with. So for
example the routines associated with maptools can project the image,
but I am not certain if they work with ggmap, or if there is a better
way to do so.

If there is an example that does something similar that you could
point me to I would appreciate it. As I said, the code below should
be stand alone, it should pull in the data and make the initial
graphic.

Thanks for any help.

-Roy M.

--
Chief Scientist, RStudio
http://had.co.nz/

On Fri, Mar 29, 2013 at 6:34 PM, Roy Mendelssohn - NOAA Federal <roy.men...@noaa.gov> wrote:
I am restricted from joining the let's see who this goes to.  please post if you get it.

# Start by specifying the desired map boundaries:
library(plyr) # makes it easier to work with *pply functions and others
library(ggplot2)
library(ggmap)
cages <-read.csv("http://barataria.tamu.edu/erddap/tabledap/CAGES_Texas_IOOS_Biology.csv?time,latitude,longitude,vernacularName,scientificName,individualCount&time>=2005-10-01T00:00:00Z&time<=2005-10-08T06:00:00Z", skip = 2, sep = ",")
# FYI - This is a >300MB file, so being able to call and query it remotely from
# R w/o local download is very convenient! By calling just the variables of
# interest the loaded data frame is only 571x6 and it loads instantly!
colnames(cages) <- c("time", "lat", "lon", "vname", "sname", "count")
cages.avg <- ddply(cages, .(lon, lat), summarize, avg = mean(count, na.rm = TRUE))

map.xlim <- c(min(cages.avg$lon)-1.5, max(cages.avg$lon)+1.5)
map.ylim <- c(min(cages.avg$lat)-1.5, max(cages.avg$lat)+1.5)

# Specify a GGPLOT2 layer for the point data, to be overlayed on any of the
# map options below:
lyr.pts <- c(geom_point(data = cages.avg, aes(x = lon, y = lat, size = avg),
                       color = "red"))

# As an alternative to the map boundaries provided above, can specify the map
# center using geocode() from "ggmap":
#map.ctr <- geocode("Port Aransas, TX") # just a guess; may need fine-tunning

# Download a nice background-layer map from the web using ggmap. This puts a
# "ggmapTemp.png" file to local drive that can be safely deleted once the final
# map is generated:
# Specifying bounding box:
bkgr <- get_map(location = c(map.xlim[1], map.ylim[1],
                                map.xlim[2], map.ylim[2]),
                   maptype = "satellite", source = "google") # "terrain"
#***Gives a warning that spatial extent is only approximate, so trial and error
#is needed because observations can be clipped if the extracted map is too
#small!
# Specifying map center:
#bkgr <- get_map(location = c(lon = map.ctr$lon, lat = map.ctr$lat),
#                    zoom = 8, maptype = "terrain", source = "google")
# Note: If Google Maps "teardrop" markers are desired, instead of get_map() use
# get_googlemap(), and specify the markers argument.

# Specify the background map layer, but do not draw anything:
lyr.bkgr = ggmap(bkgr)

# Build up map by adding elements (PODs labeled in custom order):
map.cages2 <- lyr.bkgr +
 lyr.pts +
 guides(size = guide_legend("Mean count")) +
 labs(title = "Using GGPLOT + GGMAP",
      x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude") +
 theme(axis.text = element_text(size = rel(1)))
# Export plot:
ggsave(filename = "map_cages2.png", plot = map.cages2,
      width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300) # this gives 2400 × 1800 pixels

download.file(url="http://coastwatch.pfeg.noaa.gov/erddap/griddap/erdPHsstd8day.nc?sst[(2005-10-04):1:(2005-10-04)][(0.0):1:(0.0)][(25):1:(30)][(260):1:(265)]",destfile="sst.nc")
library(ncdf4)
sstFile<-nc_open("sst.nc")
vsst <- sstFile$var[[1]]
sst<-ncvar_get(sstFile, vsst,collapse_degen=TRUE)
nc_close(sstFile)
